source_user: Advanced cluster case Mooncake-79: Analyze Mooncake-style disaggregated KV-cache or serving architecture for a long-context workload. Variant 79 must state assumptions, define a falsifiable hypothesis, name metrics, and include one failure or rollback condition.
source_assistant: An expert answer should distinguish model-domain mechanisms from runtime measurements. Required technical anchors: define prefill/decode ownership, KV placement and eviction, RDMA transfer cost, cache consistency, admission control, failure recovery, and comparison against local or conventional distributed serving. It must report topology, workload, units, baselines, confounders, and evidence needed before claiming improvement.
corrected_answer:
For Mooncake variant 79, treat disaggregated KV serving as a falsifiable, environment-dependent hypothesis rather than a guaranteed improvement. Assume a multi-node long-context service, but record model/runtime versions, GPU and NIC models, PCIe/NUMA affinity, link rate, memory limits, failure domains, prompt and generation-length distributions, concurrency, batching, and tenant boundaries; leave unknown platform facts unclaimed.

Separate prefill workers, which construct KV, from decode workers, which consume it. Define the KV block format and precision, ownership and placement, replication, cache-key scope, version/checksum validation, TTL and eviction priority, admission quotas, and control-plane state transitions. Reject stale, partial, corrupt, or unauthorized blocks. For a miss, RDMA timeout, link failure, node loss, or control-plane inconsistency, use a bounded local recompute/fallback, surface the event in logs, and make retry/rollback thresholds explicit; do not silently serve unvalidated data.

Hypothesis: at the stated concurrency and long-context mix, remote reuse reduces prefill work enough to improve p50/p95/p99 time-to-first-token and GPU utilization without violating output correctness, isolation, or SLOs. Compare with (1) local KV reuse and (2) a conventional distributed baseline using the same model, tokens, batching, placement, warm-up, and admission policy. Measure TTFT, inter-token latency, end-to-end latency, throughput in requests/s and tokens/s, cache hit/miss and reuse bytes, RDMA bytes and latency, GPU/NIC/CPU utilization, memory occupancy, evictions, queueing, retries, fallbacks, error rate, and tail distributions with confidence intervals. Attribute transfer cost separately from compute and storage cost; report units and uncertainty.

Run warm and cold trials across cache hit ratios, prompt lengths, concurrency, and failure injection. Control compression, caching policy, background traffic, thermal state, and request order. Gate rollout on no unauthorized reuse or correctness regression and on a predeclared tail-latency/error budget. If any threshold is exceeded, disable remote reuse and drain or invalidate affected entries. Evidence is insufficient without topology inventory, synchronized traces, matched baselines, versioned configuration, fault-injection recovery results, and an authorization/audit review.
risks: Mooncake implementation behavior and performance depend on unspecified versions, topology, workload, and configuration.
Remote KV introduces stale/corrupt data, RDMA failure, tail-latency, admission, and tenant-isolation risks if validation and fallback are incomplete.
evidence_required: Target topology and model/runtime/GPU/NIC/NUMA/link inventory.
Matched local-KV and conventional distributed baselines with synchronized per-request metrics, units, and uncertainty.
Fault-injection results for stale/corrupt KV, RDMA/link loss, node loss, and control-plane inconsistency.
Authorization, audit, correctness, and cross-tenant isolation review.

source_user: Advanced cluster case Mooncake-80: Analyze Mooncake-style disaggregated KV-cache or serving architecture for a long-context workload. Variant 80 must state assumptions, define a falsifiable hypothesis, name metrics, and include one failure or rollback condition.

corrected_answer:
For Mooncake variant 80, the safe tool-oriented plan is to inspect and measure the deployment, not assume that a named Mooncake mode is enabled. Assume a multi-node long-context service and collect model/runtime versions, GPU/NIC/NUMA topology, RDMA device and link inventory, memory limits, failure domains, workload distribution, concurrency, and tenant policy. Redact secrets and do not change production state during discovery.

First validate configuration and ownership: identify prefill versus decode workers, KV placement and replication, block format/precision, cache-key namespace, version/checksum checks, TTL/eviction rules, admission quotas, and control-plane transitions. Use read-only inventory and per-request trace correlation to distinguish local compute, remote KV lookup, RDMA transfer, and queueing. Reject stale, partial, corrupt, or unauthorized blocks. Define a bounded fallback to local recomputation and an operator-approved rollback/disable switch for RDMA or remote reuse; log failures and preserve auditability.

Hypothesis: under a specified long-context workload, remote KV reuse improves TTFT and tail latency at fixed correctness and isolation. Run a preregistered matrix against matched local-KV and conventional distributed baselines, with the same model, tokens, batching, warm-up, cache state, admission, and node allocation. Capture TTFT, inter-token and end-to-end latency, throughput (requests/s and tokens/s), hit/miss ratio, reused bytes, RDMA bytes/latency, GPU/NIC/CPU utilization, memory, evictions, queue time, retries, fallbacks, and errors; include units, p50/p95/p99, sample counts, and uncertainty. Stress cold misses, saturation, link loss, stale-version rejection, corrupt blocks, and node loss. Do not claim causality from aggregate latency alone: isolate transfer, compute, storage, and queueing costs.

Rollback if correctness, cross-tenant isolation, error rate, or predeclared tail/SLO thresholds regress; invalidate affected entries and return to local recompute. Evidence requires captured commands/configuration, synchronized traces, matched baseline results, fault-injection logs, and authorization/audit review. Separate network, compute, storage, and queueing costs; report units, p50/p95/p99, sample counts, and uncertainty.

Test cold/warm cache, saturation, skew, background traffic, and injected link/node/control-plane faults. Predeclare rollback gates for tail latency, error rate, failed validation, or isolation breach; disable remote reuse and drain/invalidate entries when crossed. Evidence requires topology inventory, versioned configuration, synchronized traces, matched baselines, fault-injection recovery, and security/audit review.
